root_cause.text: The papr-hvpipe driver’s ioctl/create-handle and release paths took hvpipe_src_list_lock with plain spin_lock while sharing that lock with the message-event interrupt handler, allowing same-CPU interrupt reentry to reacquire the non-IRQ-safe lock and deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says “if an interrupt fires on the same cpu, then we can enter into a deadlock,” and the patch changes papr_hvpipe_handle_release() and papr_hvpipe_dev_create_handle() from spin_lock/spin_unlock to spin_lock_irqsave/spin_unlock_irqrestore on hvpipe_src_list_lock “to prevent any race with message event IRQ.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use irq-safe locking in the hvpipe release path to avoid races or deadlocks with the message event IRQ while removing the source entry.
intent_record.what: The release handler adds a new local variable `unsigned long flags;` and replaces `spin_lock(&hvpipe_src_list_lock);` with `spin_lock_irqsave(&hvpipe_src_list_lock, flags);` while leaving the rest of the function unchanged in the shown hunk.
intent_record.how: This changes the lock acquisition to save and disable local interrupts while holding `hvpipe_src_list_lock`, preventing interrupt-context code such as the message event IRQ handler from re-entering code that may take the same lock on the same CPU and causing a race or deadlock during source removal and status reset.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restore interrupt state when releasing hvpipe_src_list_lock in papr_hvpipe_handle_release() to fix incorrect spinlock unlock handling.
intent_record.what: The code replaces two calls to spin_unlock(&hvpipe_src_list_lock) with spin_unlock_irqrestore(&hvpipe_src_list_lock, flags) in papr_hvpipe_handle_release(), both in the HVPIPE_MSG_AVAILABLE branch and the else branch.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the lock is now released while also restoring the previously saved interrupt state, rather than only unlocking the spinlock. This prevents interrupts from remaining incorrectly disabled after this critical section and keeps lock/unlock behavior consistent with a lock acquisition that saved irq flags.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect the source-list critical section with irq-safe spin locking to avoid interrupt-context races or deadlocks when creating a handle.
intent_record.what: The function papr_hvpipe_dev_create_handle() adds a local variable named flags, replaces spin_lock(&hvpipe_src_list_lock) with spin_lock_irqsave(&hvpipe_src_list_lock, flags), and replaces both matching spin_unlock(&hvpipe_src_list_lock) calls with spin_unlock_irqrestore(&hvpipe_src_list_lock, flags).
intent_record.how: This change makes the critical section save and disable local interrupts while holding hvpipe_src_list_lock, then restore the previous interrupt state on unlock. At runtime, this prevents races or deadlock scenarios that could occur if the same lock is taken from interrupt context on the same CPU while this function is executing.

intent_record.how: This changes the critical section to save and disable local interrupts while holding the lock, then restore interrupt state on unlock, preventing races or deadlocks if the same lock can be touched from interrupt context while creating and inserting a source handle.

Because interrupts are not disabled, same-CPU interrupt reentry can attempt to reacquire the lock and deadlock in the release/create-handle paths described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the lock definition and all relevant users in the create-handle and release paths. The root cause is taking a lock shared with the message-event interrupt handler using plain spin_lock instead of an IRQ-safe variant. This code defines `static DEFINE_SPINLOCK(hvpipe_src_list_lock);` and then acquires it with plain `spin_lock(&hvpipe_src_list_lock);` / `spin_unlock(&hvpipe_src_list_lock);` in both relevant paths: `papr_hvpipe_handle_release()` and `papr_hvpipe_dev_create_handle()`. In `papr_hvpipe_handle_release()`, the comment explicitly says this is to prevent races `with message event IRQ`, yet it still uses plain `spin_lock`, not `spin_lock_irqsave`/`spin_lock_irq` or equivalent. Likewise `papr_hvpipe_dev_create_handle()` uses plain `spin_lock` around `hvpipe_find_source()` and `list_add()`. Since the vulnerability is exactly that these paths share the lock with an interrupt handler and can deadlock on same-CPU interrupt reentry when using non-IRQ-safe locking, the vulnerable construct is present. No fix is present because there is no IRQ disabling/restoring around these lock acquisitions.
